description.value: The study investigated differences in brain activation during emotion regulation among schizophrenia patients, non-affected siblings, and healthy controls.

spans.text: In the current paper we investigated whether schizophrenia patients, non-affected siblings and healthy controls (HC) exhibit differences in brain activation during emotion regulation.

spans.text: FMRI data was acquired using a 3.0 Tesla whole body scanner equipped with an 8 channel SENSE head coil (Philips Intera, Best, NL).
FMRI data was acquired using a 3.0 Tesla whole body scanner equipped with an 8 channel SENSE head coil (Philips Intera, Best, NL).

The functional images were acquired by a T2-weighted echo producing 37 slices of 3.5 mm thick with no gap and the images were slightly tilted (30 degrees) to prevent artifacts due to the nasal cavities.

The functional scans were made in the axial plane (TR = 2 s; TE = 30 s; flip angle (α) 70°; FOV = 224.0, 129.5, 224.0; in-plane resolution 64×62 pixels; isotropic voxels of 3.5 mm) and were scanned interleaved.

emotion regulation task

description.value: Participants viewed emotional pictures and were instructed to attend, reappraise, or suppress their emotional responses.

spans.text: The task consisted of four main conditions: attend neutral, attend negative, reappraise and suppress, each containing 22 trials.
The task was presented with E-Prime (Psychology Software Tools Inc, Pittsburg).

stimuli.value: emotional pictures from the International Affective Picture System (IAPS)

spans.text: Stimuli were emotional pictures, extracted from the International Affective Picture System (IAPS).
attend negative
the attend negative condition

description.value: Participants viewed negative IAPS pictures and were instructed to look at them and experience the elicited emotion without attempting to change it; this served as the negative-affect control condition.

spans.text: Instructions for ‘attend’ were simply to look at the picture and not change the emotions they were feeling.
reappraise

description.value: Participants viewed negative IAPS pictures and reinterpreted each picture so that its negativity and emotional impact decreased.

spans.text: When asked to reappraise, subjects had to reinterpret the picture in such a way that its negativity decreased, making it less emotionally disturbing
suppress

description.value: Participants viewed negative IAPS pictures and attempted to suppress the elicited emotional expression, keeping a poker face so that another person could not read the emotion.

spans.text: This was illustrated by giving the example that someone else should not be able to read the emotion on the subjects’ face (i.e. keeping a poker face).
attend neutral
the attend neutral condition

description.value: Participants viewed neutral IAPS pictures and were instructed simply to look at the picture and experience the elicited emotion without changing it.

spans.text: This instruction was the same for the attend neutral condition and the attend negative condition
fixation
Fixation

description.value: A fixation cross was presented for 20 seconds during rest blocks, with one rest block following every tenth trial.

spans.text: Fourteen additional rest blocks were included, one restblock followed every tenth trial, in which a fixation cross was presented for 20 seconds (Fixation).

instructions.value: For attend conditions, look at the picture and experience the elicited emotion without changing it. For reappraisal, reinterpret the picture so that its negativity and emotional disturbance decrease. For suppression, suppress the emotion elicited by the picture so that another person could not read the emotion from the participant's face, maintaining a poker face.
